bar.x-help: The bar's thickness: thicker fills a short slot with signal.

bar_body_color.x-help: A plain bar's body, at its foot; unset uses the scene's bar body.

x-unused-when.reason: This field is coloured by its thresholds: OK, Caution and Alert.
This field is coloured by its reading: Wide, Centred and Anti-phase.
A tick is drawn in the tip colour alone.

bar_tip_color.x-help: A plain bar's tip, at its top; unset uses the scene's bar tip.

x-unused-when.reason: This field is coloured by its thresholds: OK, Caution and Alert.
This field is coloured by its reading: Wide, Centred and Anti-phase.

notice_color.x-help: What a card says when it cannot show its reading; unset uses the scene's notice.

scale_color.x-help: Scale numerals and axis labels; unset uses the scene's scale.

anchor.x-help: Where the fill starts, in the field's unit. Unset keeps the product's.

hi.x-help: The scale's high end, in the field's unit.

lo.x-help: The scale's low end, in the field's unit.

segment.x-help: A segmented style's segment size, in the field's unit. Unset keeps the product's.

x-rules: lo and hi both or neither; neither keeps the product's range
lo < hi
anchor, where set, lies between lo and hi
segment, set or else the field's, divides hi - lo
segment only on a field the product gives a segment size

scales.x-help: A field's own scale in place of its default: low, high, optional anchor and segment size.

This field's segments are sized in its unit, in Scales.

style.x-help: Fill, a tick, segments lit along the way, or one marker on segments.

tick_color.x-help: Scale ticks; unset uses the scene's tick.

ticks.x-help: Marks under the bar, evenly spaced; with 9, every other one is labelled.

title_color.x-help: Card titles; unset uses the scene's title.

track_color.x-help: An unfilled bar, arc or progress track; unset uses the scene's track.

unit_color.x-help: Units; unset uses the scene's unit.

value.x-help: The number under the name, on the name's line at the right, or not shown.

value_color.x-help: The number a card leads with; unset uses the scene's value.
